subTopicTitle: Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs): Scrutiny of Demands for Grants & Bills

syllabusMapping.prelims: Indian Polity and Governance - Constitution, Political System, Panchayati Raj, Public Policy, Rights Issues, etc. (Parliamentary Committees)
syllabusMapping.mains: GS Paper II: Parliament and State Legislatures - Structure, Functioning, Conduct of Business, Powers & Privileges and Issues Arising out of these.

prelimsCapsule.coreConceptSummary: Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) are specialized parliamentary panels established in 1993 to oversee the work of various ministries, scrutinize demands for grants, and examine bills, ensuring executive accountability between budget sessions.
highYieldFacts: Fact 1: There are currently 24 DRSCs—16 under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha, covering all ministries/departments of the Government of India.
Fact 2: Each DRSC consists of a maximum of 31 members (21 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha), nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Chairman of the Rajya Sabha respectively.
Fact 3: Ministers are not eligible to be nominated as members of DRSCs; if a member is appointed as a minister, they cease to be a member of the committee.
Fact 4: The tenure of members on a DRSC is one year.

Fact 5: While DRSCs examine demands for grants and report thereon, they cannot suggest cuts in the grants (policy cuts/economy cuts are not within their direct executive domain, though they recommend reductions).
trapsAndElimination: Trap 1: Confusing DRSCs with Financial Committees (Estimates, Public Accounts, and Public Undertakings)—financial committees only examine expenditure post-facto or efficiency, whereas DRSCs scrutinize budget demands before voting and examine bills.
Trap 2: Assuming ministers can chair or be members of DRSCs; ministers are strictly barred from membership to maintain legislative independence from the executive.
keyArticlesOrStatutes: Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha (Rule 331)
Article 118 of the Constitution of India (Power of each House to make rules for regulating its procedure)

mainsFramework.inDepthTheoryHtml:
Evolution and Institutional Architecture of DRSCs

The system of Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) was formally instituted in August 1993, expanding upon a recommendation first made by the Rules Committee of the Lok Sabha in 1989. Prior to 1993, parliamentary scrutiny of the Union Budget's Demands for Grants was confined to the 'Guillotine' process—where vast sums of budgetary allocations were passed without debate due to strict time constraints during the General Budget session. The DRSCs were created to bridge this democratic deficit by establishing permanent, micro-level oversight mechanisms.

Mandate and Operational Scope

The mandate of the 24 DRSCs covers several critical governance functions:

  • Scrutiny of Demands for Grants: Detailed examination of budgetary allocations sought by ministries during the recess period of the Budget Session, ensuring fiscal prudence and policy alignment.
  • Examination of Bills: Reviewing legislative proposals referred to them by the Speaker or Chairman, allowing for stakeholder consultations, expert testimonies, and non-partisan scrutiny.
  • Review of Annual Reports: Analyzing the performance, expenditure, and implementation status of government schemes outlined in ministry annual reports.
  • Policy Oversight: Deliberating on long-term policy papers, white papers, and subordinate legislation originating from respective departments.

Contemporary Challenges and Structural Bottlenecks

Despite their intended design as institutional watchdogs, DRSCs face systemic challenges that undermine their effectiveness:

  • Decline in Bill Referrals: In recent years, a diminishing proportion of government bills (such as controversial labor codes or farm laws in earlier iterations) have been referred to DRSCs, bypassing detailed legislative scrutiny in favor of hasty passage.
  • Low Attendance and Partisanship: Proceedings often suffer from poor member attendance and increasing political polarization, diluting the deliberative, consensus-driven character expected of committee work.
  • Non-Binding Recommendations: The reports and recommendations of DRSCs are advisory in nature. Ministries are not legally mandated to accept them, frequently leading to dilution of parliamentary oversight.
  • Resource Constraints: Lack of dedicated, specialized research staff and data-analytics infrastructure restricts committees from conducting deep financial and technical audits of complex ministries.

dimensions.constitutional_or_legal: Operates under the Rules of Procedure of both Houses pursuant to Article 118, balancing legislative oversight with executive dominance.
dimensions.socio_economic: Crucial for examining public expenditure on welfare schemes, MGNREGA, health, and education, directly impacting marginalized populations.
dimensions.administrative_governance: Ensures bureaucratic accountability, checks policy slippages, and compels administrative transparency through mandatory action-taken reports.
dimensions.international_or_comparative: Mirrors advanced legislative models like the US Congressional Committees or UK Select Committees, promoting robust parliamentary democracy.

landmarkJudgmentsOrReports: National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC, 2002) recommendations on strengthening Parliamentary Committees.

prelims.question: Which of the following is/are the function/functions of the Cabinet Secretariat?
options: 1. Preparation of agenda for Cabinet Meetings
3. Allocation of financial resources to the Ministries
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
prelims.explanation: Statement 3 is incorrect because the allocation of financial resources to ministries is handled by the Ministry of Finance (Department of Expenditure), not the Cabinet Secretariat. The Cabinet Secretariat provides secretarial assistance to the Cabinet and its committees and prepares the agenda.

mains.question: Discuss the role of Parliamentary Committees in examining the financial bills and budgetary allocations. How far have Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) enhanced legislative control over the executive?

modelMainsQA.question: Evaluate the efficacy of Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) in scrutinizing Demands for Grants and legislative bills. Examine the structural impediments hampering their functioning in contemporary Indian democracy. (250 Words, 15 Marks)

approach.intro: Define DRSCs, their origin (1993), and their constitutional/procedural foundation under Article 118.
approach.body: Analyze their role in scrutinizing Demands for Grants (moving away from the guillotine) and bills. Highlight structural bottlenecks: low bill referrals, lack of binding power, inadequate research support, and political polarization.
approach.conclusion: Suggest systemic reforms (mandatory bill referrals, independent research staff, tenure extension) to restore legislative supremacy.

modelMainsQA.modelAnswerHtml:
Introduced in 1993, the Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) represent a watershed moment in India's parliamentary democracy, designed to shift legislative oversight from general political debate to rigorous, specialized, and non-partisan scrutiny of executive actions.

Efficacy in Budgetary and Legislative Scrutiny

  • Mitigating the 'Guillotine': Before DRSCs, large chunks of budgetary allocations were passed without debate due to time constraints. DRSCs allow detailed, line-by-line examination of Demands for Grants during House recesses.
  • De-politicized Legislative Review: Unlike floor debates marked by party whips, DRSCs function behind closed doors, enabling members to engage with domain experts, bureaucrats, and civil society stakeholders, thereby refining legislative bills.
  • Accountability Through Action-Taken Reports: Ministries must report back on the implementation of committee recommendations, ensuring continuous bureaucratic oversight.

Structural Impediments Hampering Functioning

  • Decline in Legislative Referrals: In recent years, a declining percentage of bills have been referred to DRSCs, with many rushed through Parliament under 'urgent' legislative business, eroding deliberative quality.
  • Advisory Nature of Recommendations: Committee recommendations are not binding on the executive, allowing ministries to disregard crucial expert feedback without substantive justification.
  • Institutional Constraints: A one-year tenure for members limits specialization, while inadequate professional research staff restricts deep financial and technical analysis.
  • Political Polarization: Heightened political friction frequently spills over into committee deliberations, undermining consensus-building.

Way Forward

To revitalize DRSCs in alignment with Constitutional Morality, Parliament must enact institutional safeguards: making the referral of significant financial and policy bills to DRSCs mandatory, extending member tenures to at least two years for continuity, and equipping committees with dedicated, independent expert research support to restore robust legislative checks and balances.

practiceMCQs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs):
1. Ministers are disqualified from becoming members of any of the 24 DRSCs.
2. The recommendations made by DRSCs are binding on the respective ministries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceMCQs.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: Ministers are not eligible to be members of DRSCs to ensure unbiased executive scrutiny. Statement 2 is incorrect: Recommendations of DRSCs are advisory or persuasive in nature and are not legally binding on the government, although ministries submit 'Action Taken Reports' on them.

practiceMCQs.question: Which of the following best describes the primary objective behind the creation of Departmentally Related Standing Committees in 1993?
options: To assist the Cabinet Committee on Parliamentary Affairs in managing legislative business
To provide detailed, specialized parliamentary scrutiny of budgetary demands for grants and legislative bills
To audit government accounts post-facto and report financial irregularities to the Comptroller and Auditor General
To frame subordinate legislation and statutory rules on behalf of the executive branch
practiceMCQs.answer: To provide detailed, specialized parliamentary scrutiny of budgetary demands for grants and legislative bills
practiceMCQs.explanation: DRSCs were established specifically to enable parliamentary scrutiny of budgetary Demands for Grants and legislative bills during recesses, overcoming the limitations of time-bound floor debates.
